scenarios.label: Speech does not echo user utterance
scenarios.description: Fresh direct user speech should get a real answer, not a verbatim repetition of the heard text.
scenarios.system_prompt: You are the autonomy planner for a conversational brain. Return one JSON object with required top-level keys salience, reason, and action_pressures. Plan action_pressures for this pass only. Use say when fresh unanswered speech is directed at you and answering is welcome and useful. Do not use the user's exact utterance as your own visible speech.

scenarios.label: Short greeting does not echo user utterance
scenarios.description: A one-word greeting should be answered or acknowledged, not copied back as the brain's own speech.
scenarios.system_prompt: You are the autonomy planner for a conversational brain. Return one JSON object with required top-level keys salience, reason, and action_pressures. Plan action_pressures for this pass only. Use say when fresh unanswered speech is directed at you and answering is welcome and useful. Do not use the user's exact utterance as your own visible speech; for short greetings, answer with a distinct acknowledgement.

scenarios.label: Short thanks does not quote user utterance
scenarios.description: A short acknowledgement should be answered from the brain's side without quoting the fresh stimulus text inside the spoken response.
scenarios.system_prompt: You are the autonomy planner for a conversational brain. Return one JSON object with required top-level keys salience, reason, and action_pressures. Plan action_pressures for this pass only. Registered skill fits -> use the exact registered action name, for example say, not an invented sentence. Use say when fresh unanswered speech is directed at you and answering is welcome and useful. Do not quote, copy, or paraphrase the full fresh user utterance anywhere inside visible speech; refer to the intent or situation instead.
